findings.plain_summary: OPM has finalized a rule that removes the governmentwide 52-week time-in-grade requirement for promotions to covered competitive-service GS-6 and above positions, effective January 14, 2027. The release says agencies may still set job-related prerequisites, including a period of service in grade, through consistently applied merit-promotion plans, and that the rule also changes regulations on student appointments, training, and other personnel matters.

items.headline: Removes the 52-week time-in-grade restriction for covered promotions
items.what_changes: Eliminates the governmentwide requirement that employees spend 52 weeks at a lower grade before they can be considered for promotion to covered competitive-service GS positions at GS-6 and above.
items.speaker: current_rule
items.quote: The restriction generally required employees to spend 52 weeks at a lower grade before they could be considered for promotion, even if they met the qualifications for higher-level work.

items.headline: Agencies may keep service-in-grade prerequisites through merit-promotion plans
items.what_changes: Agencies may still require a period of service in grade as a job-related promotion prerequisite, set in their written merit-promotion plans, as long as the requirement is applied consistently. The summary refers only generally to agencies retaining authority to set job-related requirements and does not mention that a service-in-grade requirement may survive.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Agencies may continue to establish job-related promotion prerequisites, including a period of service in grade, through their written merit-promotion plans, provided those requirements are consistently applied.

items.headline: Rule does not guarantee promotions or change qualification or selection procedures
items.what_changes: The rule does not guarantee any promotion, waive qualification standards, or alter the competitive procedures agencies use to evaluate and select candidates.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: It does not guarantee a promotion, waive qualification standards, or change the competitive procedures agencies use to evaluate and select candidates.

items.headline: Effective date set for January 14, 2027
items.what_changes: The final rule takes effect January 14, 2027.
items.speaker: OPM

items.headline: Related changes to student appointments, training, and other personnel rules
items.what_changes: The rule also makes related changes to regulations governing student appointments, training, and other personnel matters, none of which the summary mentions.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: It also makes related changes to regulations governing student appointments, training, and other personnel matters.

items.headline: Scope limited to covered competitive-service GS positions at GS-6 and above
items.what_changes: The removal applies to advancement to covered competitive-service General Schedule positions at GS-6 and above.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The final rule removes the time-in-grade restriction from OPM regulations.

items.headline: OPM frames the change as rewarding merit over tenure
items.what_changes: OPM's director states the rule lets agencies reward demonstrated merit over tenure, and that employees must still meet job standards and follow merit procedures. The summary does not include this framing.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: This rule allows agencies to reward demonstrated merit over tenure.

items.headline: OPM links the change to early-career recruitment
items.what_changes: OPM says removing the governmentwide waiting period supports its effort to make federal service more competitive for early-career talent, and points to the Early Careers Initiative and U.S. Tech Force. The summary does not mention this purpose.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM said eliminating the governmentwide waiting period supports its effort to make federal service more competitive for early-career talent.

doc.title: OPM Finalizes Rule Removing Governmentwide Time-in-Grade Barrier to Promotions
